questions.title: How does the unified RoPE interpolation formula in Eq. (2) relate to the original RoPE definition in Eq. (1)?
questions.question_body: In the paper, Eq. (1) defines the RoPE embedding as \([\cos(n\theta_0), \sin(n\theta_0), \dots, \cos(n\theta_{d/2-1}), \sin(n\theta_{d/2-1})]\). Later, Eq. (2) rewrites the embedding with a rescale factor \(\lambda(\beta)^i\). I am confused about how the term \(\frac{n}{\lambda(\beta)^i}\) is derived from the original \(n\theta_i = n/\beta^i\). Specifically, what is the meaning of \(\lambda(\beta)^i\) and how does it incorporate the extension ratio \(s\)?

questions.title: What is the intuition behind keeping the first \(\hat n\) tokens un‑interpolated (Finding 2)?
questions.question_body: The authors claim that the initial \(\hat n\) tokens should receive "less interpolation" because they attract large attention scores. How does reduced interpolation for early positions help the model, and why does the optimal \(\hat n\) depend on the target extension length? Are there any empirical analyses (e.g., attention heatmaps) that support this hypothesis?

questions.title: Why does the monotonicity constraint \(\lambda_i \le \lambda_{i+1}\) improve search efficiency?
questions.question_body: During evolution‑based search, the authors enforce that rescale factors increase monotonically with RoPE dimension. I understand this follows NTK theory, but I’m unclear how this constraint reduces the number of perplexity evaluations. Does it prune infeasible candidates, or does it also guide the mutation/crossover operators? How much speed‑up is reported compared to an unconstrained search?

questions.title: How is the progressive extension strategy able to reach 2048k with only 1k fine‑tuning steps?
questions.question_body: The paper mentions fine‑tuning LLaMA2 for 400 steps at 128k and then 600 steps at 256k, after which a second search yields 2048k without further training. Why does this two‑stage fine‑tuning suffice? Is the model already capable of handling 512× extension after 256k fine‑tuning because of preserved RoPE information, or does the second search compensate for remaining gaps?

questions.title: What exact loss function is used during the evolutionary search when optimizing for perplexity?
questions.question_body: The optimization problem (Eq. 4) minimizes a loss \(\mathcal{L}\) over samples longer than the target length, and later they say they use perplexity as a proxy. Is \(\mathcal{L}\) simply the average negative log‑likelihood (i.e., cross‑entropy) over next‑token predictions on a small validation set? Are any regularization terms added to discourage extreme \(\lambda_i\) values?

questions.title: How does LongRoPE handle dynamic inference lengths shorter than 8k?
questions.question_body: During inference, the authors state that if the sequence length is less than 8k they "update RoPE with the searched rescale factors." Does this mean they switch to a different set of \(\lambda_i\) learned for short contexts, or do they simply truncate the existing factors? How is this switching implemented without recomputing embeddings for each request?

questions.title: Why does YaRN underperform PI and NTK on PG19 in non‑fine‑tuned settings?
questions.question_body: Table 1 shows YaRN’s perplexity spikes after 7k tokens on PG19, even though YaRN is supposed to be more flexible than PI/NTK. Is this because YaRN’s three‑group heuristic fails to reach the required 8k length, or does its extrapolation strategy cause instability for certain datasets? Could a different grouping of dimensions improve YaRN’s performance here?

questions.title: What is the role of the extra "short context recovery" search after extending to 2048k?
questions.question_body: The authors note performance degradation on the original 4k window after a 512× extension and run a second evolution search with reduced maximum \(\lambda\). How exactly does this second search alleviate crowding of position embeddings? Does it re‑fit only low‑frequency dimensions, or does it also adjust \(\hat n\)?

questions.title: How do the authors evaluate passkey retrieval accuracy over million‑token contexts?
questions.question_body: The passkey task places a five‑digit number randomly inside a document up to 2048k tokens. I’m unsure how they generate prompts, query lengths, and how they determine whether the model retrieved the correct passkey (e.g., exact match vs. fuzzy match). Also, what decoding settings (temperature, top‑p) are used that might affect retrieval?

questions.title: Can LongRoPE be applied to models that use absolute sinusoidal positional encodings instead of RoPE?
questions.question_body: The paper repeatedly states that LongRoPE works for any LLM based on RoPE. If an LLM uses classic sinusoidal embeddings or learned absolute embeddings, could a similar evolutionary search be performed on those embeddings, or are there fundamental obstacles (e.g., lack of rotational invariance) that prevent direct transfer?
